mbm-1401.clue: I always leave the wooden chair empty.
mbm-1401.quote: At our first garage show we had five people and a squeaky chair in the audience. The chair squeaked right on the last beat. Now our band gives it a front-row seat at every rehearsal.

mbm-1402.clue: I bring a spoon for the sandbar.
mbm-1402.quote: There’s a smooth sandbar I can reach only by kayak. I use a teaspoon to scoop a little channel and watch the water race through. After lunch the tide erases the whole river I made.

mbm-1403.clue: I keep my canoe seat low for a reason.
mbm-1403.quote: I like to see the world at the height of the water lilies. One morning a dragonfly rode the rim of my hat from blossom to blossom. I barely touched the paddle until it flew off.

mbm-1404.clue: I roll the dice into a paper town.
mbm-1404.quote: My nephew folded little houses around our board game to catch runaway dice. On my best roll both dice went in the post office. I asked whether that meant I should expect a letter.

mbm-1405.clue: I play the racing game with the curtains open.
mbm-1405.quote: My sister tapes a paper ribbon to the monitor whenever I reach the finish. A breeze through the window lifts it like a real race flag. The pixel cars seem a little faster on windy days.

mbm-1406.clue: My starting line rolls up when I’m done.
mbm-1406.quote: My first coach taught me to mark my foot position on a gym towel before lifting. I still roll it out carefully. Everybody else sees two ink marks. I see a very dependable starting line.

mbm-1407.clue: I gave the first arepa a handle.
mbm-1407.quote: My niece asked for an arepa shaped like a little bag. We worked a loop into the dough and tucked the filling beneath it. The loop broke right away, so she ate the handle before the bag.

mbm-1408.clue: I can spot our raft from the bridge.
mbm-1408.quote: Our crew tied a bright yellow sponge to the bow for bailing. My friends on the bridge said they could see it from a mile away. We held it up like a trophy after the soggiest turn.

mbm-1409.clue: I lift the paddle at the swallows’ bridge.
mbm-1409.quote: When our canoe passes beneath the old bridge, the swallows wheel above us like little dark commas. I rest my paddle and try to read the sentence before they scatter.

mbm-1410.clue: I set my watch by the little weight room.
mbm-1410.quote: The wall clock there runs four minutes slow. At first I kept correcting it. Now I enjoy four whole extra minutes of stretching while the late sun creeps from one dumbbell to the next.

mbm-1411.clue: I carry one feather in a leather sleeve.
mbm-1411.quote: I stamped a fine line down the middle of a narrow leather case to echo a feather’s shaft. It protects the gull feather my little brother found on our first trip to the shore.

mbm-1412.clue: I made one square rough as bark.
mbm-1412.quote: My quilt of our apple tree has a strip of rough brown corduroy for the trunk. My niece shuts her eyes and climbs its branches with two fingertips. She always finds the bright red patch at the top.

mbm-1413.clue: I saved the little bells for the finish.
mbm-1413.quote: I tied tiny bells to two juggling bags and kept the third silent. With my eyes closed I can hear the missing beat circling in the pattern. My neighbor dances to it on the other side of the fence.

mbm-1414.clue: I still make a space for the vanished cup.
mbm-1414.quote: I mark three spots on the tablecloth for my cup trick. My little brother drew a tiny chair inside the middle spot. He says that’s where the missing cup waits between shows.

mbm-1415.clue: I get up early for an empty platform.
mbm-1415.quote: The local train pushes a little ridge of mist before it reaches our stop. I drew that ridge with a gray pencil for weeks before I managed to draw the engine that made it.

mbm-1416.clue: I take the address off the little bell.
mbm-1416.quote: While sightseeing I walked a whole street listening to different shop-door bells. A silversmith’s bell sounded like two raindrops in a bowl. I wrote down the address so I could hear it again on the way home.

mbm-1417.clue: I sew my name into the hem in pictures.
mbm-1417.quote: I embroidered a little wave into the hem of the jacket I made. My surname is too long to fit on the label. My mother spotted that wave and knew whose sewing she had in her hands.

mbm-1418.clue: I turned our recipe into a quilt.
mbm-1418.quote: I stitched round red tomatoes, a green leaf and a square of cheese into a kitchen hanging. My nephew likes tracing the pattern pieces with me. He still insists the last square should have more cheese.

mbm-1419.clue: I once won an entire wooden lemon.
mbm-1419.quote: At the tart-eating contest the prize was a lemon carved from wood. It sits in the fruit bowl with the real ones. I find out who’s been looking for a snack when I hear the little knock.

mbm-1420.clue: I keep a wool fish in the first-aid kit.
mbm-1420.quote: I crocheted a bright little fish with an empty belly to hold sticking plasters. My nephew says a scraped knee improves the moment the fish opens its mouth. The fish has a wonderful bedside manner.

mbm-1421.clue: I lift the roof to see the forecast.
mbm-1421.quote: My fantasy deck has a whole stack of storms, clear skies and sudden fog. I painted their little box like a weather station and open the lid just a crack to reveal the forecast.

mbm-1422.quote: I paint a tiny white lighthouse on my thumb and little breaking waves across the other nails. When my younger cousin holds my hand upright the harbor appears. Close my fist and the tide goes out.

mbm-1423.clue: I sharpen the pencil before I tune in.
mbm-1423.quote: I tried copying a radio friend’s call sign with a worn pencil and made a perfectly useless smudge. She repeated it slowly and sent a card with a drawing of a giant pencil. It hangs over my dial.

mbm-1424.clue: I trust the little golden moth.
mbm-1424.quote: I traded for a fantasy card with a moth that can hide one creature in the dark. I saved the tiniest creature in my deck with it and won. Now my friends all check the lamps before we deal.

mbm-1425.clue: I carry a white envelope for the shadows.
mbm-1425.quote: I slip the empty envelope under flowers and pebbles when I take pictures so the little shadows stand out. In my favorite print a single dandelion seed casts the shadow of a palm tree.
